title: Fibre products commute with inverse limits
statement:
Let $(X_i\xrightarrow{\gamma_i} S_i \xleftarrow{\delta_i} Y_i)_{i\in I}$ be a compatible inverse system of schemes [def-pc-scheme]: the transition maps of the three inverse systems commute with the displayed structural maps. Assume all indicated inverse limits exist. The fibre products are those of [def-pc-fibre-product]. Then the canonical map

$$
\varprojlim_i(X_i\times_{S_i}Y_i)\longrightarrow
\bigl(\varprojlim_iX_i\bigr)\times_{\varprojlim_iS_i}
\bigl(\varprojlim_iY_i\bigr)
$$

is an isomorphism.

proof.text: For every scheme $Z$, a morphism $Z\to\varprojlim_i(X_i\times_{S_i}Y_i)$ is, by the universal property of the inverse limit, a compatible family of morphisms $Z\to X_i\times_{S_i}Y_i$. By the universal property of each fibre product, this is exactly a compatible family of triples $(x_i,y_i,s_i)$ with $x_i:Z\to X_i$, $y_i:Z\to Y_i$, and $s_i:Z\to S_i$ satisfying $s_i=\gamma_i\circ x_i$ and $s_i=\delta_i\circ y_i$, compatible with the transition maps of the three systems.

Applying the universal property first to the limits $\varprojlim_iX_i$, $\varprojlim_iY_i$, and $\varprojlim_iS_i$, and then to their fibre product, identifies morphisms $Z\to(\varprojlim_iX_i)\times_{\varprojlim_iS_i}(\varprojlim_iY_i)$ with the same compatible triples. Under both identifications the canonical comparison map sends a triple to its componentwise pair, so it induces the identity on this set for every $Z$. The two universal constructions therefore give mutually inverse morphisms, and the canonical map is an isomorphism.
